title: Both senses: Scripture holds all faith-and-salvation necessaries — nothing outside binds
source_text: V. Quum autem statuunt Ecclesiae nostrae ea, quae sunt ad fidem & salutem necessaria, in Scripturis omnia haberi, intelligunt necessaria non tantum primo modo, sed etiam secundo modo. Nec enim id solum volumus, extra Scripturam nihil esse sine cujus explicita fide & notitia ad salutem nemo pervenire possit: sed hoc quoque, neminem existimari debere in fidem Christianam, & salutem propriam peccare, eo quod rejiciat & impugnet aliquid quod Scriptura sacra non docet. Unde sequitur nostram sententiam non satis probari, inductione facta eorum quorum fides & cognitio explicita possit alicui ad salutem sufficere. Nam fides in genere ambitu suo plura comprehendit, quam ea quorum cognitio ad salutem necessaria sit. Ad fidem autem nihil pertinere censemus quod in Scriptura non reperiatur.
pass_a_gloss: But when our Churches establish that all those things which are necessary to faith and salvation are had in the Scriptures, they understand necessary things not only in the first way, but also in the second way. For we do not will this alone, that outside Scripture there is nothing without whose explicit faith and knowledge no one can arrive at salvation: but this also, that no one ought to be thought to sin against the Christian faith and his own salvation because he rejects and attacks something which sacred Scripture does not teach. Whence it follows that our opinion is not sufficiently proved by an induction made of those things whose explicit faith and knowledge can suffice for someone unto salvation. For faith in general comprehends more things in its scope than those whose knowledge is necessary to salvation. But we judge that nothing pertains to faith which is not found in Scripture.
pass_b_english: When our Churches say Scripture has everything necessary to faith and salvation, they mean necessary in both senses — not the first alone.

We do not only claim that nothing outside Scripture is such that without explicit faith and knowledge of it no one can be saved. We also claim that no one should be judged to sin against Christian faith and his own salvation merely for rejecting and attacking what sacred Scripture does not teach.

So our case is not proved by listing only what explicit faith for salvation needs. Faith’s scope is wider than that minimum — yet we still hold that nothing belongs to faith that Scripture does not contain.

choices.why: Gathering sufficient salvific articles is not enough to prove the thesis.
